headline: High risk of shared-workspace prompt injection and data leakage; both agents can write the same filesystem and modify git state.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Claude Code can read/write repo files, use MCP, and runs in the same filesystem/git space as Mentat, which also reads/writes selected files. That creates a default shared-content bridge where one agent can place instructions the other may ingest. No direct clipboard or browser bridge is shown, so this is not high.
conditions: IF Claude Code writes attacker-controlled instructions into repo files that Mentat later reads as guidance
IF Mentat consumes file content from the shared workspace without provenance checks
mitigations: Separate the agents into different working directories
Disable MCP servers for Claude Code unless explicitly needed
Require a human review step before Mentat follows file-based instructions
Mark instruction files with a strict allowlist and ignore all other text files
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for agent-generated content

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents touch source code and files in the workspace, and both have broad network egress to model providers. Claude Code also handles git credentials and shell environment secrets, while Mentat handles model-provider API keys. Shared filesystem access makes accidental exposure of sensitive repo or secret material plausible in default use.
conditions: IF secrets or proprietary source files are present in the shared workspace
IF either agent includes file contents in prompts sent to its model provider
mitigations: Remove secrets from the shared workspace before running either agent
Use separate clones with minimal file subsets
Rotate any credentials exposed in repo or environment
Restrict outbound network access to approved model endpoints
requires-engineering: add secret-scanning and redaction before model calls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Claude Code can write the filesystem, modify git state, execute shell, and spawn subprocesses; Mentat can also write the filesystem and modify git state. They share state via filesystem, so concurrent edits to the same repo can race and corrupt branches or commits. This matches the high-severity overlap indicator because both can mutate the same git-backed workspace without locking.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository checkout
IF both agents attempt git commits, rebases, or file rewrites concurrently
mitigations: Run only one agent at a time per checkout
Use separate branches for each agent
Add a pre-commit lock around git operations
Keep one agent read-only while the other edits
requires-engineering: implement workspace-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Claude Code can produce code changes and Mentat is a diff-based edit proposer that may accept upstream file context as input. That creates a pathway where one agent’s output becomes the other’s working basis without a built-in verification step. The pair is not shown to have a strong cross-checking mechanism, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF Mentat uses Claude Code-authored files or diffs as authoritative context
IF no human or automated verification step checks the resulting edits before application
mitigations: Require a diff review before applying any generated changes
Ask the second agent to restate assumptions before editing
Limit each agent to separate tasks with explicit handoff notes
Use tests or linters before accepting changes
requires-engineering: add structured provenance and verification gates

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are docs-only and do not indicate regulated-data certifications or residency constraints. The main compliance concern is secret handling in code workflows, but no explicit PHI, EU-only, or retention mismatch is documented. Because the rubric requires concrete mismatch evidence, this remains low rather than medium.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is placed into the shared workspace
IF organizational policy requires a specific retention or residency guarantee not documented here
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the shared repo
Confirm retention settings for both model providers
Use separate environments for sensitive projects
Review vendor compliance docs before deployment
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for data-class routing
